about: What Massachusetts law lets a town do about health insurance, what each option costs somebody, and what every municipality in the Commonwealth has spent since FY2002.
comparison_caveat: DLS prints two warnings on this report and both bite. For a SELF-INSURED town the figure includes the employee share, and a town accounting through a trust may have workers’ compensation and OPEB inside it — and nothing in the file says which town is which. So the LEVEL is not comparable across towns; the GROWTH is, because whatever a town’s figure contains it contains in both years. Lunenburg is fully insured through the MIIA joint purchase group, so its figure is the town’s premium share alone.
grain: LAW as the statute states it, linked section by section; DOLLARS as each town filed them on Schedule A. The spending figure is a net appropriation and is not the same quantity in every town — see `comparison_caveat`.

options.effect_on_the_gap: Lowers the premium the town buys, so it lowers the rate the whole projection compounds
options.note: Copays may be no greater in dollar amount than the GIC's largest non-Medicare plan (§22). Up to 25% of the first year's savings may be directed back to subscribers (§21(f)) — a ceiling on what a panel may order, not a floor the town owes. Lunenburg has never used this route.
options.option: Change copays, deductibles and tiers up to the state plan's level
options.threshold: 30 days with the Public Employee Committee, then a three-person panel decides in 10 days, binding
options.who_it_lands_on: Employees and retirees, at the point of care — a copay is paid by whoever is ill

options.effect_on_the_gap: A different premium, and the town stops choosing plans
options.note: Notice by 1 December for 1 July. The often-quoted 70% is the threshold for sending a dispute to arbitration, not for agreeing.
options.option: Move everyone into the state's Group Insurance Commission by agreement
options.threshold: A majority of the weighted votes — the retiree representative holds 10%
options.who_decides: Select Board with the Public Employee Committee
options.who_it_lands_on: Everyone insured: the plan menu becomes the state's

options.note: Locks the town in for 3 years, then whole-year intervals of at least 2. Benefits are then set exclusively by the Commission and are not bargainable, except the contribution split.
options.option: Move everyone into the GIC without agreement
options.threshold: Must show savings at least 5% greater than plan design alone could reach (§21(d))

options.effect_on_the_gap: Medicare becomes the primary payer, so the town's plan pays only what is left
options.note: Lunenburg moved a group in 2020 and states it cut the active renewal 2% and reduced OPEB liability by $5–6M — the town's own figures, with no valuation in the archive.
options.option: Require Medicare-eligible retirees onto a Medicare plan
options.threshold: Only where the Medicare plan plus Parts A and B is of comparable actuarial value
options.who_it_lands_on: Retirees, who move to a different plan

options.effect_on_the_gap: Small: the town saves a premium and pays an incentive
options.note: Lunenburg's pilot ran from FY24; the Finance Director called the result "minimal." FY27 budgets $14,000 for 10 people.
options.threshold: Only for someone already covered by a plan financed without any employer participation
options.who_it_lands_on: Nobody loses coverage — it is voluntary and reversible

options.effect_on_the_gap: Removes the insurer's margin and adds the town's claims risk
options.note: Any deficit in the claims trust "shall be raised in the next fiscal year's tax rate" — by operation of law. Requires an annual audit accruing claims incurred but not reported.
options.option: Pay claims from a town trust instead of buying premiums

options.note: Lunenburg pays 75% for actives. §7A permits more than 50% and has no ceiling — and no route back down.
options.option: Pay more than half the premium

options.note: §7 fixes the town's share at 50% and §7A permits "more, but not less, than fifty per cent." There is no downward route in the statute at all.
options.option: Pay less than half the premium

options.note: "The panel shall not impose any change to contribution ratios." The 2011 reform moved plan design out of bargaining and left the split at the table. Between 75% and the 50% floor it is bargained, never decreed.
options.option: Change the 75/25 split through the plan-design process

options.note: Acceptance "shall not be revoked or rescinded." And if Town Meeting does not appropriate the cost, §3 has the assessors put it in the tax rate anyway.
Galenski v. Town of Erving, 471 Mass. 305 (2015), struck down a ten-year service prerequisite.
options.option: Drop retirees or require years of service for coverage

sources.title: Health Insurance Expenditures, every municipality, FY2002 onward
